scope: Explicit reviewed exact source-syntax, platform FFI and test dispositions; not a file-wide, rule-wide, platform-wide or unsafe-code exemption.
normalization: Decode UTF-8, remove one leading BOM, normalize CRLF and CR to LF. File sha256 hashes the complete normalized text, retaining its final newline. line_sha256 hashes the start line without its newline. span_sha256 hashes lines startLine..endLine inclusive joined by LF, without a trailing LF.
provenance_note: Raw report SHA identifies the reviewed input only; a future complete SARIF run must still be evaluated and is not required to have this SHA.

review_axes.correctness: All 107 existing dispositions are retained. During the current upstream integration, 106 spans remain byte-identical after LF/noBOM normalization; the LSP cleanup disposition is narrowed to the root-reviewed inline signal_kill expression. Changed-file dispositions are uniquely anchored by their recorded containing function; new analyzer findings still require separate review.
review_axes.readability: Every exception names its containing function and records the native contract; source or span changes invalidate the record.
review_axes.architecture: Platform-specific FFI and bench/test modules remain separated; no scanner rules are disabled.
review_axes.security: Broad syntax rules remain enabled. Exact reviewed command-input parsing, FFI and owned-test false positives are fingerprinted. New findings, errors, suppressions or missing/changed fingerprints fail closed.
review_axes.performance: Read-only drive/RSS/process queries avoid helper-process creation; benchmark diagnostics do not enter ordinary builds.

This disposition covers the recorded unsafe block only, not arbitrary process admission.

signal_kill: Root integration review approved this narrowed inline process-group signal. The existing owned SharedChild supplies the group ID established by CommandExt::process_group(0); libc::kill takes integer IDs and no raw buffer or untrusted pointer. ESRCH is an accepted child-exit race; other signal errors propagate before the child kill/wait path. Windows retains the owned Job Object cleanup. This disposition covers only the recorded inline unsafe expression.

kill_takes_down_process_group: Recorded process-group cleanup/test calls operate on owned child/group IDs; the kernel APIs take integer IDs and the test probes its own spawned grandchild. Test pre_exec is confined to the process-cleanup fixture.
